MAKEHUMAN GRAPHICAL ASSET SOURCES

The pedestrian characters adapt CC0 MakeHuman graphical assets. This includes
the hm08 anatomical base mesh, native skin weights, age/body/facial morphs,
core fitted garments and footwear, hair cards, eye meshes, eyebrow meshes,
and source diffuse/normal surface maps. Added role accessories and cloth
panels were built for this batch. Character surfaces were recoloured, atlas
packed, and combined; geometry was fitted and reduced, then rigged/exported
with a shared Mixamo-named skeleton and animated for this pack.

Official repository:
https://github.com/makehumancommunity/makehuman

Base mesh:
https://github.com/makehumancommunity/makehuman/blob/master/makehuman/data/3dobjs/base.obj

Official system asset-pack catalogue, listing the included CC0 resources:
https://static.makehumancommunity.org/assets/assetpacks/makehuman_system_assets.html

Downloaded official asset pack:
https://files2.makehumancommunity.org/asset_packs/makehuman_system_assets/makehuman_system_assets_cc0.zip

Asset licensing:
https://github.com/makehumancommunity/makehuman/blob/master/LICENSE.ASSETS.md
https://github.com/makehumancommunity/makehuman/blob/master/LICENSE.md

The source assets identify MakeHuman Team contributors, Data Collection AB,
Joel Palmius and Jonas Hauquier, among others. Original per-asset and per-file
credits are retained in the official source distribution. Graphical assets
are released under CC0 1.0 Universal, separately from the application's code
licence. A copy of the asset licence is included beside this document.

EXPANSION PACK REFERENCES
Vendor and officer bodies adapt the same CC0 assets; equipment, birds, props, tram, drone and mech additions were constructed for this pack. Original URB-07 surface maps were reused for the matching enemies. No reference photographs are embedded.

Police visual/reference research:
https://www.brigadamilitar.rs.gov.br/upload/arquivos/202505/30174309-ruapbm-2025.pdf
https://brigadamilitar.rs.gov.br/pecas-historicas
https://www.alegretetudo.com.br/conheca-o-conceito-por-tras-do-novo-fardamento-da-brigada-militar/
The generic light-green uniform follows the user direction, not a certified replica of any current official uniform.

Historical tram reference:
https://www2.portoalegre.rs.gov.br/carris/default.php?p_secao=61&reg=2
https://memoriacarris.blogspot.com/2013/04/novos-amigos.html
The tram is a generic decorative interpretation, not a dimensionally documented restoration.
